articles.title: PEP Schoolv2 opens Montessori IGCSE school in Hyderabad - Telangana Today
articles.content: NRI View Point cartoon My Space Reviews Education Today Property Lifestyle Home | Hyderabad | Pep Schoolv2 Opens Montessori Igcse School In Hyderabad PEP Schoolv2 opens Montessori IGCSE school in Hyderabad PEP Schoolv2 has opened a Montessori IGCSE school at PEP Kokapet in Hyderabad, starting with Grades 1 to 6 and admissions for Grades 1 to 4 at its expanded 350-student campus. By Telangana Today Updated On - 26 November 2026, 04:41 PM Telangana: PEP Schoolv2, a network of Montessori schools across Bangalore and Hyderabad, announced the opening of a Montessori IGCSE school at its Hyderabad campus, PEP Kokapet. The school will begin with a Montessori Elementary programme for Grades 1 to 6, with academics taught in classes of six, and will grow into a high school on the IGCSE pathway. To make room, PEP Kokapet is moving to larger premises in Kokapet with capacity for 350 students, where the established Montessori preschool and the new school will share one campus. Admissions are now open for Grades 1 to 4 for families who want to join immediately or from the next academic year. Higher grades will be added as students move up. Elementary will run through Grade 6, while high school will run from Grade 7 to Grade 10. PEP Schoolv2’s model starts from the belief that every child should be known as an individual, taught at the level they are ready for, and prepared for a future that will ask far more of them than exam scores. Admissions follow a consultative, mutual-fit process that includes a school tour and time for the child in a classroom. Families can learn more and book a visit at pepschoolv2.com or by calling 91 91602 71717. articles.title: India's First Newspaper Returns After 246 Years With Stories Of Scandal and Colonial Secret
articles.content: Hicky's Bengal Gazette Online, Colonial Calcutta's Secrets in India's First Newspaper Authored by : Girish Shukla Updated: Nov 26, 2026, 15:00 IST Share In December 1778, Philip Francis, a member of the governor-general's council in Calcutta, climbed a bamboo ladder into the bedroom of a young married woman and was caught there. Her husband sued and won 50,000 sicca rupees. Two years later a weekly paper printed the case all over again, this time with a dissenting judge's doubts about the evidence. The paper was Hicky's Bengal Gazette, India's first newspaper, and its surviving pages, scattered for nearly two and a half centuries, can now be read online. The American historian Andrew Otis, who holds a PhD in journalism, has launched hickysgazette.com, a searchable archive that puts every known surviving issue in chronological order alongside transcriptions. Anyone who enjoys history through its gossip and its grudges will lose an evening to it. A Paper That Lasted Two Years James Augustus Hicky, an Irishman, printed the first issue on 29 January 1780. It came out every Saturday under the motto "Open to all parties, but influenced by none", and the last issue appeared on 30 March 1782. In those two years Hicky produced 121 issues and a prospectus, 464 pages in all. James Augustus Hicky Challenged the British with India's First Newspaper No institution holds a complete set. Otis found seven incomplete collections in six archives across India, the United Kingdom, Germany, Australia and the United States. He fitted them together into the fullest run of the paper assembled since Hicky stopped printing. He started during a Fulbright fellowship in Kolkata. The National Library of India had copies but would not let him photograph or scan them, so he bought paper photocopies, took them home and scanned them himself. His best find came later, in the record room of the Calcutta High Court, where a special edition dated 25 June 1781 had lain for more than 230 years. In it Hicky argued for the freedom of the press, after the governor-general's council had moved against his paper. Mocking the Mighty Hicky kept clear of politics at first. Within months he was going after the most powerful men in Bengal, usually by nickname, which made him harder to sue and more fun to read. The chief justice, Elijah Impey, was "Poolbundy", a reference to allegations about contracts for repairing Bengal's embankments. Justice Robert Chambers became "Sir Viner Pliant", a jab at his academic background and his alleged closeness to the governor-general, Warren Hastings, whom Hicky called a tyrant. He accused the Swedish missionary Johann Zachariah Kiernander of misusing money meant for educating orphans. He even used the classified columns. One mock notice reported that sincerity and honesty had gone missing, and another advertised for someone who would neither offer nor accept bribes. Some of the jokes need footnotes now. The complaints behind them, about officials who seemed to be enriching themselves, need none. The Francis Affair Francis was Hastings's bitter rival on...

articles.title: 10 Former Chief Justices of India Inaugurate India's First Chief Justices of India Museum at JGU
articles.content: In an extraordinary gathering of judicial leadership, 10 former Chief Justices of India came together, in person or virtually, to inaugurate India’s first Chief Justices of India Museum at O.P. Jindal Global University (JGU) on the eve of Constitution Day. The inauguration marked a significant moment in the preservation of India’s judicial heritage, honouring the individuals and the institutions that have shaped the Republic’s constitutional journey. Envisioned as “Guardians of the Republic,” the Museum brings judicial history into conversation with art, technology and personal testimony, inviting visitors to explore how justice shapes individual lives and the destiny of a nation. Across five galleries, it features more than 280 busts of Supreme Court judges, models of 25 High Courts, 22 language tapestries, 20 interactive biographical pillars and 20 defining judgments, alongside a holographic courtroom and an extensive collection of artworks, sculptures and installations. The inauguration brought together Hon’ble Mr. Justice M.N. Venkatachaliah, Hon’ble Mr. Justice B.N. Kirpal, Hon’ble Mr. Justice S. Rajendra Babu, Hon’ble Mr. Justice K.G. Balakrishnan, Hon’ble Mr. Justice P. Sathasivam, Hon’ble Mr. Justice R.M. Lodha, Hon’ble Mr. Justice Dipak Misra, Hon’ble Mr. Justice Sharad A. Bobde, Hon’ble Mr. Justice U.U. Lalit and Hon’ble Mr. Justice B.R. Gavai. Their collective presence lent exceptional significance to an occasion dedicated to preserving judicial memory and inspiring future generations. Envisioned as “Guardians of the Republic,” the Museum brings judicial history into conversation with art, technology and personal testimony, inviting visitors to explore how justice shapes individual lives and the destiny of a nation. The inauguration brought together former Chief Justices MN Venkatachaliah , BN Kirpal , S Rajendra Babu , KG Balakrishnan , P Sathasivam , RM Lodha , Dipak Misra , SA Bobde , UU Lalit and BR Gavai . Hailing the occasion, Naveen Jindal , the Founding Chancellor of JGU said, “The Constitution of India is the enduring foundation of our Republic, embodying the ideals of justice, liberty, equality and fraternity. India’s first museum dedicated to the Chief Justices extends the vision of our Constitution Museum by honouring the Supreme Court’s guardianship of these constitutional values. My own journey to secure every citizen’s right to fly the national flag taught me that the Constitution is not a distant text but a living promise, kept alive by an independent judiciary that listens to the citizen. The Supreme Court’s recognition of that right in 2004 remains, for me, a lasting reminder of what our courts mean for the freedom of ordinary Indians.” Articulating the vision behind the Museum, Prof (Dr) C Raj Kumar , the Founding Vice Chancellor of JGU said, “The Chief Justices of India Museum explores justice as an evolving idea, tracing how the Supreme Court of India, through its Chief Justices and Judges, has shaped the nation’s constitutional democracy. It presents the Office of the Chief Justice as a living institution that has interpreted, protected and strengthened the Constitution through moments of national transformation. By bringing together law, history, memory and public engagement, it celebrates the collective legacy of successive Chief Justices and reflects on how their leadership has shaped the constitutional journey of independent India.” The former Chief Justices reflected on judicial independence, constitutional values, legal education and the rule of law, connecting the Museum’s commemorative purpose with the responsibilities of future generations. Justice MN Venkatachaliah said that the single largest factor in India’s progress and economic growth has been the idea of freedom, democratic ideals and the rule of law. "The museum will nurture legal education and future law practitioners. articles.title: Karnataka Explores India's First Sustainable Coastal Data Centre In Mangaluru - BW People
articles.content: The Karnataka government is examining the possibility of establishing what it hopes will be India's first sustainable coastal data centre in Mangaluru, with Electronics, IT-BT and E-Governance Minister Priyank Kharge assessing a 49-acre site near Tannirbhavi Blue Flag beach. The proposed location is being evaluated for its suitability for a data centre, with around 20 acres of the identified land parcel available for permanent construction under existing Coastal Regulation Zone (CRZ) regulations. Following his inspection of the site on Wednesday, Kharge said the state would prepare a white paper outlining the activities permitted at the location and the infrastructure requirements to enable private sector participation. The proposal forms part of Karnataka's broader push to develop environmentally sustainable digital infrastructure as demand for computing capacity rises amid the expansion of artificial intelligence (AI). Karnataka Evaluates Tannirbhavi Site For Sustainable Data Centre The state is exploring the development of a sustainable data centre at Tannirbhavi, with the proposed project expected to be assessed against coastal regulations, infrastructure requirements and environmental considerations. Kharge said a white paper would be prepared in consultation with the Mangaluru City Corporation Commissioner and the Zilla Panchayat Chief Executive Officer. The document is expected to outline the activities permissible at the site and the basic infrastructure needed to attract private investors. The identified land spans 49 acres, of which approximately 20 acres can be used for permanent construction under the prevailing CRZ norms. The feasibility exercise is intended to establish whether the location can accommodate a sustainable data centre while complying with regulatory requirements and minimising environmental impact. Karnataka's Sustainable Data Centre Policy 2026-31 The proposed development is aligned with the Karnataka Sustainable Data Centre Policy 2026-31, which received Cabinet approval during a meeting held in Mangaluru on September 18. Kharge said the state had replaced its earlier policy framework with a sustainability-focused approach aimed at limiting water and energy consumption by data centres. The policy comes as the rapid expansion of AI infrastructure is increasing demand for computing facilities, power and cooling systems. Karnataka is seeking to encourage infrastructure development while ensuring that data centres operate with a reduced environmental footprint. The state's approach places sustainability at the centre of its data centre development strategy, with an emphasis on reducing resource consumption and mitigating environmental risks associated with large-scale infrastructure. Karnataka Pushes Coastal IT Expansion Beyond Bengaluru The data centre proposal also forms part of Karnataka's efforts to broaden its technology ecosystem beyond Bengaluru. Kharge said the state had prepared a blueprint connecting Mangaluru, Manipal and Udupi as part of a broader regional IT development strategy. The coastal region currently generates IT exports worth approximately Rs 5,000 crore, according to the minister. He also noted that companies were exploring the possibility of establishing Nano Global Capability Centres (GCCs) in the region. The proposed regional development plan is aimed at strengthening the coastal belt's technology ecosystem, attracting new investments and expanding employment and business opportunities beyond Karnataka's established technology hub in Bengaluru. articles.title: Toyota Innova HyCross Flex Hybrid review: India's first E20–E85 hybrid MPV is big ...
articles.content: Published By : Vipin Vijayan Last Updated: 26 November 2026, 01:48 PM IST 5 min Share Follow us on The Toyota Innova HyCross Flex Hybrid combines a flex-fuel engine with strong hybrid technology. Here is a detailed look at its price, mileage, safety and cabin features. ❎ Toyota’s all-new Innova HyCross Flex Hybrid is not just another refresh of India’s most trusted family MPV. It is the country’s first Flex Hybrid Electric Vehicle, combining a locally made flex-fuel engine with a strong hybrid system that can run on petrol-ethanol blends from E20 to E85. The result is a spacious, premium seven- or eight-seater that promises flexibility at the pump, hybrid efficiency and a more modern cabin -- though its price and size mean it remains firmly aimed at buyers who want space, comfort and long-term ownership rather than outright performance. To advertise here, Contact Us The big change is under the bonnet. The Innova HyCross Flex Hybrid pairs a TNGA 2.0-litre flexi engine with Toyota Hybrid System and an e-Drive transmission, delivering a combined 147 kW, or 197.13 hp. The key selling point is fuel flexibility. The vehicle can run on any ethanol blend from E20 to E85, giving owners the freedom to choose between conventional petrol blends and higher ethanol content. Toyota claims 22.58 km/l on E20, a figure that will matter to fleet operators and families covering long distances. The hybrid system is self-charging, meaning there is no plug-in requirement. Drivers can choose between EV, Eco and Power modes depending on traffic, terrain and the need for a bit more urge. How it drives Toyota has not positioned the Innova HyCross as a performance MPV, and the numbers reflect that. The 197.13 hp combined output is respectable for a vehicle of this size, and the e-Drive transmission should deliver smooth, linear acceleration typical of Toyota’s hybrid systems. The real test will be how the flex-fuel engine and hybrid system work together across different ethanol blends. Toyota says it conducted nationwide testing across city, highway, hilly and rough-terrain conditions, as well as extreme climates, to validate efficiency, robustness and reliability. For buyers, the promise is simple: no range anxiety, no dependence on charging infrastructure, and the flexibility to adapt to whatever fuel is available. That is a compelling proposition in a country where ethanol blending is still evolving. Design: Bolder, but familiar The refreshed exterior gives the Innova HyCross a more contemporary face. A new front bumper and grille, redesigned projector LED headlamps, double-stacked LED daytime running lights and a three-dimensional lower grille with integrated fog-lamp bezels give it a sharper, more SUV-like stance. At the rear, double-stacked combination lamps and a wider visual treatment aim to make the MPV look more planted and premium. Alloy wheels, a roof-end spoiler, rear chrome garnish and wheel-arch extensions round out the package. It is still recognisably an Innova—which is both a strength and a limitation. The design evolution is noticeable but not radical, and buyers looking for a dramatic visual change...

articles.title: K'taka explores setting up India's first sustainable coastal data centre: Priyank Kharge
articles.content: Business K'taka explores setting up India's first sustainable coastal data centre: Priyank Kharge PTI • 26 November 2026 Karnataka government explores setting up India's first sustainable data centre in coastal Mangaluru, with a 49-acre site identified at Tannirbhavi as part of its push to expand the state's IT ecosystem beyond Bengaluru. The Karnataka government is evaluating the feasibility of setting up India's first sustainable data centre along the coast of Mangaluru, Electronics, IT-BT and E-Governance Minister Priyank Kharge said on Wednesday. Kharge inspected an identified 49-acre land parcel near the Tannirbhavi Blue Flag beach here. Speaking to reporters after the site visit, the minister said permanent construction is permissible on approximately 20 acres of the plot under existing Coastal Regulation Zone (CRZ) norms. "We are exploring whether the country's first sustainable data centre can be established at Tannirbhavi. A white paper detailing permitted activities and required basic infrastructure will be prepared in consultation with the Mangaluru City Corporation Commissioner and the Zilla Panchayat CEO to facilitate private sector participation," Kharge said. The initiative aligns with the 'Karnataka Sustainable Data Centre Policy 2026-31, which the State Cabinet approved during its meeting in Mangaluru on September 18. Kharge noted that the state scrapped its earlier policy to introduce a sustainable framework, claimed to be the first of its kind in India that mandates minimal water and energy consumption to prevent adverse environmental impacts amid rising AI-driven infrastructure demands. Highlighting plans to expand the IT footprint beyond Bengaluru, Kharge said a blueprint integrating Mangaluru, Manipal, and Udupi has been drafted. The coastal belt currently records Rs 5,000 crore in IT exports, and companies are showing interest in setting up Nano Global Capability Centres (GCCs) in the region, he added. articles.title: Govt eyes coastal Mangaluru for India's first ' green ' data centre - The Hans India
articles.content: Govt eyes coastal Mangaluru for India’s first ‘green’ data centre The Hans India Update: 2026-11-26 06:21 IST Govt eyes coastal Mangaluru for India’s first ‘green’ data centre Looking to decentralise Karnataka’s technology sector beyond Bengaluru while addressing the heavy resource footprint of artificial intelligence infrastructure, the State government has initiated a feasibility assessment to establish India’s first sustainable data centre along the Tannirbhavi coast in Mangaluru. Electronics and IT-BT Minister Priyank Kharge on Wednesday inspected a 49-acre coastal land parcel near the Tannirbhavi Blue Flag beach, accompanied by Dakshina Kannada Zilla Panchayat Chief Executive Officer Narwade Vinayak Karbhari and Mangaluru City Corporation (MCC) Commissioner Rahul Ratnam Panday. Navigating CRZ norms Because the proposed site lies along the sensitive coastline, land-use regulations remain a primary consideration. Mr. Kharge clarified that under Coastal Regulation Zone (CRZ) norms, permanent structures can be raised on roughly 20 acres of the 49-acre expanse. To give prospective private investors clarity on regulatory clearances and utility readiness, the government plans to issue a comprehensive white paper. “Once we detail what is permissible on the remaining land and map out the requisite infrastructure with the MCC and Zilla Panchayat, providing that white paper to private firms will make execution seamless,” the Minister told reporters. Policy pivot for the AI era The Tannirbhavi proposal is anchored in the Karnataka Sustainable Data Centre Policy 2026–2031, cleared by the Cabinet during its special session in Mangaluru on September 18. According to Mr Kharge, the government revoked its previous data centre policy after industry consultations underscored the unsustainable water and power demands of conventional facilities. “Whether we like it or not, the AI era has arrived, and data centres are its backbone. Building them responsibly without compromising the environment or future generations is our obligation,” he said, adding that while undersea data centres are being tested in the U.S. and Europe, Karnataka is pioneering low-resource coastal facilities leveraging future submarine cable landing infrastructure. Beyond Bengaluru The project forms part of a wider regional blueprint covering the Mangaluru–Manipal–Udupi cluster. With the coastal belt already generating ₹5,000 crore in IT exports, the State is actively courting private capital to set up Nano Global Capability Centres (GCCs) and tap into local engineering talent. Alongside the recently approved Marine Biotech Policy, the government expects the five-year IT roadmap to accelerate investment once private players come on board, Kharge said. articles.title: Wow! India's AI -powered police stn to make debut at Panjagutta - The Hans India
articles.content: Wow! India’s AI-powered police stn to make debut at Panjagutta MM Farooqui Update: 2026-11-26 04:47 IST Wow! India’s AI-powered police stn to make debut at Panjagutta Hyderabad: Telangana Director General of Police (DGP) CV Anand said Panjagutta Police Station to become India’s first Artificial Intelligence (AI)-powered police station and would soon be officially inaugurated as an AI-based police station under the pilot initiative. The DGP, along with Hyderabad City Police Commissioner Dr Mahesh Muralidhar Bhagwat, conducted a surprise inspection of Panjagutta Police Station on Wednesday to review the ongoing technical works and assess the implementation of the AI-based policing system. In a major step towards modernising policing through technology, Panjagutta Police Station is being transformed into the country’s first Artificial Intelligence (AI)-powered police station, where AI technology will be integrated into every stage of policing, from receiving complaints to preparing charge sheets. As part of the pilot project, the police station will integrate advanced AI technology into its day-to-day operations to improve efficiency, streamline procedures and enhance public service delivery. Accompanied by Khairatabad Zone DCP Shilpavalli, ACP Murali Krishna and Panjagutta Inspector Jahangir Yadav, the officials inspected the AI infrastructure being installed at the station and reviewed the progress of the project at the ground level. During the inspection, the senior officers interacted with complainants visiting the police station and enquired about their experiences in lodging complaints and getting their grievances addressed through the AI system. They also monitored the performance of police personnel and examined how staff members were using AI tools in carrying out their duties. articles.title: Lucknow's KGMU To Develop India's First Indigenous Brain Atlas For Early Detection Of ...
articles.content: Lucknow: Early signs of brain disorders could soon be detected more accurately with the help of an indigenous scientific benchmark for the Indian population. King George's Medical University (KGMU) is spearheading the ‘Manas Mandal’ project to develop a digital atlas of the Indian brain by studying 700 healthy individuals from different parts of the country. The initiative aims to establish a standard reference for the structure and functioning of the Indian brain, helping doctors identify changes associated with neurological disorders at an early stage. मस्तिष्क अनुसंधान को मिलेगी नई दिशाKGMU में ब्रेन कनेक्टोम एटलस पर शोध से भारतीय मस्तिष्क का डिजिटल मानचित्र तैयार होगा। AI और MRI तकनीक आधारित यह पहल स्ट्रोक, ब्रेन ट्यूमर और डिमेंशिया के अध्ययन को नई दिशा देगी।#BrainResearch #KGMU #HealthInnovation https://t.co/j5g7r1ShAM — UP Swasth (@UP_Swasth) November 25, 2026 AI To Aid Brain Mapping Dr Durgesh Kumar Dwivedi of KGMU said the absence of an India-specific brain atlas had made it difficult to accurately compare brain scans of Indian patients with existing international databases. The proposed atlas will help doctors understand the differences between healthy and diseased brains and assess the impact of various neurological conditions. Artificial intelligence (AI) will play a key role in the project by standardising MRI data collected from different hospitals and machines, allowing researchers to compare scans on a common platform. The study will examine brain structure and connectivity between different regions. 700 Healthy Volunteers To Be Studied The research will involve 700 healthy men and women aged between 20 and 60 years. To ensure adequate representation, participants will be selected from diverse professional and social backgrounds and linguistic groups, including Hindi, Urdu, Bhojpuri, Bengali and Tamil speakers. The AI-based model will subsequently be tested on 50 patients each suffering from brain stroke, severe head injury, brain tumours and dementia, including Alzheimer's disease. This will help researchers understand how these conditions affect brain structure and connectivity. The study will use conventional MRI scans as well as diffusion and functional MRI techniques. Researchers will also examine biological markers in blood, memory, cognitive abilities and genetic factors to build a comprehensive understanding of the Indian brain. However, the brain atlas will not independently confirm a disease. It will serve as a reference tool to help doctors identify abnormalities and improve clinical assessment. Smartphone-Based Screening For Rural Areas The second phase of the Manas Mandal project proposes a smartphone-based cognitive screening tool to improve access to preliminary brain health assessments in rural and remote areas. People suspected of having neurological disorders often have to travel to major cities because many rural areas lack MRI facilities and specialist neurologists. The proposed mobile-based tool will screen memory, attention and comprehension, helping identify people who may need further medical evaluation. articles.title: India gets agent-native Git forge with local data residency via Entire-Sarvam tie-up
articles.content: India gets agent-native Git forge with local data residency via Entire-Sarvam tie-up IANS November 25, 2026 1:27 PM Share on | New Delhi, Nov 25 (IANS) Developer platform Entire -- founded by former GitHub Chief Executive Officer Thomas Dohmke -- on Wednesday announced a partnership with Indian artificial intelligence (AI) startup Sarvam to launch India's first agent-native Git forge with local data residency capabilities. The collaboration will allow software developers and enterprises to host code within India while running AI-powered coding agents using models developed and served by Sarvam, addressing growing demand for sovereign AI and data localisation solutions. Under the partnership, code repositories hosted on Entire's platform can remain in India, while AI inference for agent-assisted software development will be provided through Sarvam's full-stack AI infrastructure. "I believe India can set the standard for agent-human collaboration at a scale we've never seen, producing more code than anywhere on earth," said Dohmke. "As India pursues AI sovereignty, that code and the inference behind it need to stay at home, especially for organisations in highly regulated industries," he added. The integration will enable developers using Entire's Trails workflow platform to access Sarvam's models for AI-assisted coding, code review and software development tasks while keeping inference and data processing within India. Vivek Raghavan, co-founder of Sarvam, said the partnership would allow Indian enterprises to run AI-driven development workflows while maintaining local control over both code and AI infrastructure. "India should be able to manufacture intelligence here, and the country's developers should be able to use it in the tools they rely on to build software," Raghavan said. The companies said the offering is designed particularly for organisations operating in regulated sectors where data residency and compliance requirements are critical. In addition, Entire said developers would be able to create, migrate and host private repositories in India, making the country the primary region and source of truth for software development data. --IANS ag/

articles.content: The initiative, called the Integrated Secure Infrastructure Solution, is intended to address risks arising from the increasing digitalisation of substations. KPTCL said modern facilities rely on digital systems for monitoring, control and operations, making cyber security a critical part of protecting grid infrastructure and maintaining reliable transmission services. The programme includes OT firewalls, network segmentation, zero-trust access controls and advanced threat-prevention systems. It also provides for security scanning of devices used across the network, including USB drives, laptops and other removable media, to identify and limit potential threats entering operational systems. Monitoring of the network will be centralised through KPTCL’s Data Centre and Disaster Recovery facilities. Energy Minister KJ George said the initiative would strengthen the security of Karnataka’s transmission network, while KPTCL Managing Director Ram Prasath Manohar said bringing all 1,474 substations and six ALDC locations under a unified OT architecture would establish a stronger framework for cyber resilience in India’s power transmission sector. The programme is designed as a multi-layered protection system for the operational technology that directly controls the transmission network. Its coverage of substations, control centres and connected devices is intended to improve visibility of cyber risks and support a coordinated response to threats affecting critical power infrastructure.
